text: Maya held her backpack straps tight at the big red school door. Her knees felt wobbly, like jelly on a plate. Pip hiccupped three golden sparkles. "Wobbly knees just mean something new is starting," he whispered. Maya took one slow breath and stepped inside.

At snack time, Leo said Maya's drawing looked like a squished potato. Maya's cheeks went hot and her eyes got stingy. She told Ms. Rosa, who knelt down to listen. "Unkind words can hurt," Ms. Rosa said softly. "Thank you for telling me."

Grandpa's blue racer zoomed to the last square, just ahead of Maya's red one. "I lost!" Maya groaned, flopping onto the rug. Pip flopped too, belly up like a little balloon. "Losing feels grumbly," he said. "But we still had fun racing, didn't we?"

Stomp, stomp, STOMP! Maya's angry feeling was big and hot, like a teakettle ready to whistle. Mama crouched beside her. "Let's be dragons and blow the hot air out," she said. Maya huffed three long, slow breaths, and her stomps got smaller and smaller.

Bun-Bun the floppy rabbit was missing. Not under the bed, not by the bathtub, not even in the Pillow Fort. Maya's chin wobbled and a tear slid down. Papa hugged her close. "It's okay to feel sad," he said. "Tomorrow we'll look again together."

At recess, three friends played tag, and nobody asked Maya to join. She sat on the bench feeling small and left out. Pip peeked from her pocket. "You could ask," he squeaked. Maya took a breath and called, "Can I play too?" "Yes! You're it!"

Maya had snatched the purple crayon right out of Nia's hand. Now Nia's lip was trembling, and Maya's tummy felt twisty. She held the crayon out. "I'm sorry I grabbed. You can use it first." Nia smiled, and the twisty feeling melted like butter.

Bubbles the goldfish wasn't swimming in his bowl anymore. Mama said gently that Bubbles had died, and his little body had stopped working. Maya cried, and Mama held her close. "We'll always remember him," Mama said. Together they planted a yellow flower on Moonberry Hill.

When Baby Theo got a shiny new rattle, everyone clapped. Maya crossed her arms. A prickly green feeling poked inside her chest. "That's called jealous," Papa said. "Everybody feels it sometimes." Then he winked. "Want to be Theo's rattle teacher?"

BEEP-BEEP-BEEP went the fire alarm during the practice drill. Maya covered her ears, and Pip hiccupped a whole cloud of sparkles. "It's only practice, friends," Ms. Rosa said calmly. "Hold hands and follow me." Everyone walked outside in a nice slow line.

Thunder rumbled softly, far away over Moonberry Hill. Maya snuggled into the Pillow Fort, a dinosaur bandage on her scraped knee from recess. "Big feelings day," she yawned. Pip tucked his tail around her. "And a big, brave heart," he whispered. Soon they were fast asleep.
Tomorrow is Maya's first day of kindergarten and she's really nervous that nobody will play with her. Can you tell her a story about being brave at a new school?
Maya's goldfish Bubbles died this morning and she cried all afternoon. Can you make a gentle bedtime story that helps her feel a little better?
A girl in Maya's class told her she wasn't invited to her birthday party and Maya came home heartbroken. Tell a story about feeling left out and still being a good friend.
